clue.text: Actor's last to enter stage, with reserve — one offers alternative lines to speak

definitions.text: one offers alternative lines to speak

indicators.note: the actor's final letter is told to go into the stage word, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a stage is a phase, as in a stage of development

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Actor's is the one wanted here

parts.note: to reserve a table is to book it

explanation.surface: A theatre direction: the actor makes a late entrance, holding something back, while someone feeds alternative lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts R, the last letter of Actor's, inside PHASE to make PHRASE. The definition plays on 'lines to speak': a tourist's guide gives you foreign sentences to say instead of your own.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller's guide lists ready-made sentences in a foreign tongue, supplying alternative lines for the user to speak.

clue.text: Turned up before church the colour of apoplexy?

indicators.note: turned here means flipped round, so the little word beside it is read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone turning up before church goes red in the face, as if about to burst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses the clue's own word 'up' to give PU. 'Turned up' looks like one phrase meaning arrived; it splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplexy makes the face flush a dark purplish red, the shade of this brownish-purple colour name.

clue.text: Arrest initiators of this odd encounter

parts.note: to run someone in is slang for arresting them

indicators.note: initiators are the starting letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A police officer reflects on the strange meeting that led to an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone by chance is to come across or meet them unexpectedly.

clue.text: Rover, assisting others to rove?

parts.note: Rover is a typical dog's name; this dog helps blind people get about freely

explanation.surface: A wanderer who helps other people wander.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover is the stock name for a pet dog, so the clue describes a dog whose job is to let a sightless owner move about.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained guide animal leads a blind person, letting them roam about independently: a Rover helping others rove.

clue.text: Gathering consuming cold meat with a trace of light sauce

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so one word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ham is a meat

indicators.note: only a trace, the first letter, of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A party where people tuck into cold cuts with a little light dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' wraps the gathering word round C and the meat; a bee is an old word for a social get-together, as in a quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the classic white sauce of French cooking, made from a roux and milk.

clue.text: Stubborn Conservative avoiding difficulty and ultimate in ignominy

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so a letter is left out of the word for difficulty

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in a difficulty

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A hardline Tory dodges trouble and comes out in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes C from CORNER, leaving ORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal American word for cantankerous and obstinate, a mulish temperament.

clue.text: Source of funds, with zero invested? It's very little

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: an ATM, a cash machine, is a source of money
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A financial question: if nothing is put in, what returns could there be? Hardly any.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' puts O inside ATM.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element is proverbially tiny, the very type of something minute.

clue.text: Architect finally arranged most of a certain window feature

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: to run an event is to arrange it, so arranged gives ran

indicators.note: most of means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: some can mean a certain, as in some person

explanation.surface: An architect, at last, sets out most of a particular detail for a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SOME to SOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbar dividing a window, or the small window above a door, is a standard architectural element of glazing.

clue.text: There's Irish in the team I support (Liverpool and so on)

indicators.note: in shows one piece sitting inside another

parts.note: the team I support is my side
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: A football fan notes there is an Irish player in their team, Liverpool among others.
explanation.walkthrough: MERSEYSIDE is the English metropolitan county around Liverpool, and the definition makes it a region taking in that city and its neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: The metropolitan county containing Liverpool plus surrounding towns, so the city and others like it.

clue.text: Patronise dive after study

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
to dive is to drop or descend

explanation.surface: Someone talks down to another after looking into a grubby bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' looks like a seedy bar; here it is the verb meaning plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone with lofty superiority is to stoop graciously, as if from a higher place.

clue.text: Expectation of scoring will get one in a couple

indicators.note: in says the next piece goes inside the other

parts.note: par is the expected score on a golf hole
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A golfer reckons that meeting the expected score will earn a place among a twosome.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome, two of a kind matched together, is a synonym for a couple.

clue.text: Study session still popular with good college girl

parts.note: even can mean still, as in even better
in means fashionable or popular
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A popular study period still attended by a good student from college.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson held after work hours for adult learners is a period of tuition, a session of study.

clue.text: Party to end in ennui? Definitely not in Paris

indicators.note: end in points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: non is French for no

explanation.surface: Someone bored stiff refuses a French party: certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a celebration, but 'Party to' means sharing knowledge of.
explanation.definitionFit: Being privy to a secret, sharing knowledge of a plan, is the idiomatic sense of party to.

clue.text: Upstart lawyer, knowing no limits, penning Volume One

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals
having no limits means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a barrister is a lawyer in court
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ambitious young lawyer, boundlessly clever, writes a first volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no limits' strips BARRISTER to ARRISTE; 'penning' puts VI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A social climber who has recently gained wealth or status is called a parvenu or upstart.

clue.text: Modern composer runs into little musical sound, we hear

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bit is a little
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a whistle is a musical sound

explanation.surface: A contemporary composer works some piping into a short piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Harrison Birtwistle was a modern English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrison Birtwistle, an English composer of avant-garde works, is a leading twentieth-century figure in music.

clue.text: I had backed second opera company about English opera

parts.note: I had shortens to I'd

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: about means round, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera

clue.text: A problem in returning hostility

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A recurring difficulty breeds resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses SUM IN, giving NIMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity or ill will towards someone is the sense of this Latin-derived word for enmity.

clue.text: Claim leadership in Yorkshire town is deposed

indicators.note: leadership points to the leading letter of the town
deposed means removed from power, so that letter goes

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.walkthrough: Harrogate is a spa town in Yorkshire; its leading letter H is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something for oneself without right is to assume or seize it, laying claim to it.

clue.text: Dog is briefly seen in one drawing

indicators.note: seen in shows the short piece placed inside the longer one

parts.note: a tower is one that tows or draws along
is shortened becomes 's, an S

explanation.surface: An artist's dog appears in one of the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests art; here it means pulling, so one drawing is a tower, one who tows.

clue.text: We take effect around special location on the Net

indicators.note: around shows one piece wrapping round the other

parts.note: to bite is to take effect, as a policy bites

explanation.surface: We see a policy start to bite around a special place online.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of pages at one address is a place on the internet, a web destination.

clue.text: Boozer finally tucking into dark, dark rum?

definitions.text: Boozer finally tucking into dark, dark rum?

indicators.note: tucking into means slipping inside, so the letter goes into the other word

parts.note: dun is a dull dark brown

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
rum means odd, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.definitionFit: A habitual heavy drinker is a sot or boozer, here shown downing dark rum.

clue.text: Articles about mastery and power shown by Roman leader

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the rest

parts.note: a and a are two indefinite articles
a grip on something is mastery of it

explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's general and admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa was a Roman statesman and commander who won at Actium.

clue.text: Yes please, not half (excitedly nodding)

explanation.definitionFit: Nodding off means dozing, so a drowsy person is nodding, ready for bed.

clue.text: I'm changing blog or I will create uproar

clue.text: Spend wildly, being depressed

clue.text: Surfers' Paradise: California's foremost bay creeps ruined

explanation.definitionFit: The online world is the ideal home of those who browse the web, internet surfers.
